findings: Packager selects exactly the three predeclared existing gzip roles and pins their prior selected identities and metadata; it performs no gzip processing, data decoding, model call or Git mutation.

Input identities are checked before and after opaque splitting. Ordered chunks are at most4000000B, content-addressed bySHA256, and duplicates are reused only after matching length/hash/file identity. Complete ordered concatenation must reproduce each original identity.
Both identical compressed trace roles retain separate role paths while sharing their verified chunk sequence. This does not collapse the downstream independent raw-capture roles.

Restorer requires a completed packaging receipt, exact bound helper and manifest, exact three-role path inventory, safe nonsymlink paths, all ordered-concatenation checks and all existing-target checks before any installation.

Matching existing gzip files are preserved; differing files cause failure. Absent outputs are written to individually fsynced temporary files and installed with link(), which cannot overwrite a concurrent existing target. Installed identity is checked and temporary files are removed.

The subsequent reviewed raw-asset restorer remains responsible for restoring two distinct raw-capture inodes and their original byte identities; canonical capture validation remains required before scientific use.
scope: Narrow read-only source review of opaque compressed-byte splitting and restoration. No helper or scientific execution. Saved-byte packaging validation is separately attributed to transport_publication_review.json.
